items.title: 'Noah Doe' Lawsuit Triggers Dormant Bitcoin Movement
points: 411.45 BTC ($33.4M) moved on October 19 from an address dormant since September 2013, when the BTC was worth just $54,000.

The address is one of 39,069 dormant wallets named in a New York lawsuit by pseudonymous plaintiff 'Noah Doe' and two Wyoming companies, who argue the coins constitute abandoned property and should be seized.
Coins moved to a new unlabeled address rather than an exchange, suggesting an attempt to complicate the abandoned-property claim.
Galaxy Research notes dormant wallets named in the lawsuit are moving at an accelerating pace month-over-month, suggesting coordinated activity to defeat the legal challenge.

items.title: Quantum Computing Threats to Crypto Security
points: Ethereum Foundation researcher Justin Drake warns AI could crack ECDSA signatures (the cryptographic math that proves control of a wallet's private keys) before quantum computers can, forcing urgent industry upgrades.

Zcash developer Zakura found that publishing a single shielded address publicly creates a future quantum vulnerability: attackers could later link every payment that wallet ever received, despite Zcash's privacy design.
The threat isn't immediate, but core infrastructure teams are beginning design work on quantum-resistant alternatives.

items.title: Market Positioning: Institutional Accumulation Continues
points: Tom Lee's Bitmine added 12,535 ETH ($30M) this week, continuing a weekly buying streak despite a broader market selloff pressured by $108 oil and 5% bond yields.
Bitcoin tested support at $81,890 (up 1% in 24 hours), with traders watching a coiled, trendless market.

items.title: Sparkasse's Bitcoin Entry: Retail Banking Goes Crypto
points: Germany's Sparkasse, a cooperative retail banking network serving 40 million customers, plans to add Bitcoin to its balance sheet.
This makes it one of the largest traditional banks to formally integrate Bitcoin holdings, shifting from viewing it as speculative to a legitimate institutional reserve asset.
The move mirrors recent adoption trends among corporations and endowments, further normalizing Bitcoin across financial sectors.

items.title: Institutional Accumulation Continues
points: Strive Bitcoin Trust added 1,223 Bitcoin to its holdings, reflecting continued organized capital inflows from structured investment vehicles.
Corporate and trust-based buyers remain net accumulators despite market volatility, suggesting long-term positioning over speculation.

headlines: Germany's Sparkasse, a 40-million-customer retail bank network, plans to add Bitcoin to its balance sheet, signaling major institutional adoption in traditional banking.
Strive Bitcoin Trust acquired 1,223 Bitcoin, expanding its holdings as corporate demand for BTC continues to accelerate.
Multiple bitcoin-holding entities maintain accumulation strategies, demonstrating sustained institutional confidence in long-term value.

sections.title: Sparkasse's Bitcoin Entry: Retail Banking Goes Crypto
points: Sparkasse serves 40 million customers across Germany's cooperative banking network, making this one of the largest traditional banks to formally integrate Bitcoin holdings.
The move represents a fundamental shift in how legacy financial institutions view cryptocurrency—from speculative asset to legitimate institutional reserve.
This adoption pattern mirrors recent trends among major corporations and endowments, normalizing Bitcoin across diverse financial sectors.
